title: The pictures for where words sit down a box answer to a name
goal: The three little pictures that set whether text sits at the top, middle or bottom of its box have no name at all: a screen reader announces nothing for them, and an automated walk cannot press them. The three beside them, for left, center and right, do have names. Give the down row the same.
notes:
A plain Image(systemName:) hands the segment whatever the system calls the symbol, and align.vertical.top/center/bottom carry no description at all, so PlaytestPanelPress.name(ofSegment:) returns nil and the segment is skipped. ArrowheadStyle.glyph shows the fix: build the Image through NSImage(systemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:) and set accessibilityDescription. Doing the same to the Across row would rename its press targets from "align center" to "Center", which mixed-one-look-walk.json and any other walk pressing them would have to be updated for. Found on 2026-09-06 while giving each picture its own tooltip.

Done 2026-09-06. Fix is TextVerticalAlign.glyph in LayersPanel.swift (NSImage(systemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:) at pointSize 11, weight .medium, description also assigned explicitly). 11/medium is what Image(systemName:) already draws at inside .pickerStyle(.segmented) + .controlSize(.small), proven by a 4x offscreen pixel diff in both appearances. The Across row was left on the system's own descriptions on purpose, so the two rows read differently in a panel listing.
acceptance: A panel listing names all three pictures in the Down row, the way it already names the three in Across
A scripted walk can press one of them by name
The pictures themselves do not change

log.note: Reproduced before changing anything: NSImage(systemSymbolName:) for align.vertical.top/center/bottom returns an image whose accessibilityDescription is nil, while text.alignleft/center/right come back as "align left"/"align center"/"align right". So the Down row genuinely had no name and was skipped, exactly as the notes said.

Adversarial pass on the idea. Shortest version that delivers the value is one glyph accessor on TextVerticalAlign, same recipe as ArrowheadStyle.glyph; nothing else needs to move. Deliberately did NOT rename the Across row: it already works, and renaming it would churn segment-tooltips-walk.json and mixed-one-look-walk.json for no user gain. Cost of that call is that the two rows answer to different-looking names ("align left" vs "Top"); documented in the harness doc with an instruction to read a panel listing rather than guess.

Guarded acceptance item 3 ("the pictures do not change") before writing app code: an ImageRenderer harness rendered the same small segmented picker with Image(systemName:) and with the NSImage glyph at 4x, light and dark. Both come out 0 differing pixels of 73728. Control run at pointSize 16 bold differs by 8640 px, so the harness is sensitive and 11pt/medium is the right match.

Shipped: TextVerticalAlign.glyph in Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, used by the Down picker. Walk step added to Scripts/playtest/segment-tooltips-walk.json pressing "Bottom" in "Down" by name. docs/design/playtest-harness.md corrected: it claimed the vertical segments came out as "align vertical top", which was never true.

Verified on the probe app (Screen Recording granted, real -sc.png captures). Panel listing before the press: Top (already on), Middle, Bottom, each with its own tooltip; after the press: Bottom (already on), and the walk state reads "down bottom x1". Cropped the real capture of both rows: the Down glyphs sit at the same weight, size and track as the Across ones. All 4139 tests pass.

No audit written. This names three buttons for a screen reader and unblocks a walk; there is nothing a person can sit down and judge, so a try/evaluate report would be noise. The change is covered by the segment-tooltips walk instead.

The Down row's three pictures now carry their own names (Top, Middle, Bottom) via NSImage accessibility descriptions in LayersPanel.swift, so a screen reader reads them and a walk can press them. segment-tooltips-walk.json presses Bottom by name; verified on the probe app with real captures (listing goes Top already on -> Bottom already on, state reads 'down bottom'). Pictures unchanged: 0 of 73728 differing pixels in a 4x offscreen diff, light and dark. 4139 tests pass. Pushed as c121dba.
